sentences.text: The only known fossil is a single vertebra featuring a small body and large hollows typical of rebbachisaurids — a group of sauropod dinosaurs.
Based on this fragment, scientists estimate the animal reached 15 meters in length, stood 4.5 meters tall, and weighed 10 tons.
The sole specimen, a dorsal vertebra, was collected in 1889 by Hugo Zapałowicz.
Hungarian paleontologist Franz Nopcsa von Felső-Szilvás first described this specimen in a 1902 publication.
Argentine paleontologist Sebastián Apesteguía later named the species Nopcsaspondylus alarconensis in 2007.
It is classified within the family Rebbachisauridae.
Its parent group is classified as Khebbashia.
The dinosaur lived during the Early Cretaceous (Albian) in the Candeleros Formation of Neuquén, Argentina.
It lived approximately 89 million years ago during the Coniacian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now South America.
The fossil record for this period dates from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago.
Researcher Lerzo (2026) reevaluated the species and considered it a nomen dubium, a term for fossils too fragmentary to define a valid species.
